facts.text: AeroHand is the SDK's hardware class; its constructor opens a serial port with a 0.01 s read and write timeout and takes the port and baudrate as arguments.
AeroHand copies joint_lower_limits, joint_upper_limits, actuation_lower_limits and actuation_upper_limits from AeroHandConstants onto the instance.

set_joint_positions accepts 16 or 7 joint positions in degrees, expands the compact 7-joint form to 16, clamps each position to the joint limits and sends CTRL_POS after normalizing the actuations to the uint16 range.
set_joint_positions catches a SerialTimeoutException from the CTRL_POS write, prints it and returns without raising.

set_actuations accepts 7 actuations in degrees, clamps each to the actuation limits and sends the same CTRL_POS frame, printing a SerialTimeoutException instead of raising it; the docstring warns that the thumb actuations are not independent and an uncoupled command can derail the thumb tendons.
get_actuations sends GET_POS, requires the full 16-byte reply and the GET_POS opcode, and returns None on a short read or an unexpected opcode.
get_joint_positions_compact returns 7 joint positions in degrees and returns None when get_actuations returns None.
get_actuator_speeds sends GET_VEL and converts each signed raw value with the factor 0.732 RPM.
get_actuator_currents sends GET_CURR and converts each signed raw value with the factor 6.5 mA.
get_actuator_temperatures sends GET_TEMP and returns the unsigned values directly as degrees Celsius.
set_speed takes an actuator id 0..6 and a speed 0..32766, sends SET_SPE and waits for the matching acknowledgement.
set_torque takes an actuator id 0..6 and a torque value 0..1000, sends SET_TOR and waits for the matching acknowledgement.
calibrate_mid takes an actuator id 0..6, sends CALIBRATE_MID and requires firmware protocol version 1, a non-error status and non-sentinel raw values.
AeroHandConstants declares the 16 joint names and the 16 joint lower and upper limits.
AeroHandConstants declares the 7 actuation names and the 7 actuation lower and upper limits.
The SDK GUI's 'Set to Open Position' button calls on_zero_all.
on_zero_all sets the sliders to 0.0 and sends list(self.hand.joint_lower_limits) through set_joint_positions.

The firmware control opcodes include HOMING, SET_ID, TRIM, CALIBRATE_MID, CTRL_POS, CTRL_TOR, GET_POS, GET_VEL, GET_CURR, GET_TEMP, SET_SPE and SET_TOR; it declares no stop, disable, brake or torque-off opcode.
The firmware handles CTRL_POS by switching to position mode when needed and calling SyncWritePosEx with the per-servo speed, acceleration and torque limits; it does not acknowledge the frame.
The firmware handles CTRL_TOR by raising each torque magnitude to at least HOLD_MAG, signing it toward the grasp direction and writing it in torque mode.
While homing is busy the firmware loop reads and discards every host byte.
The ROS 2 node creates subscriptions on the right/left joint_control or actuator_control topics, by control_space, and publishers on the right/left actuator_states topics.

safe_state.description: No acknowledged stop: the firmware has no stop, disable, brake or torque-off opcode and does not acknowledge a CTRL_POS frame, and set_joint_positions swallows a serial write timeout. The e-stop writes the joint lower limits (the GUI's open pose, a finger motion, not a hold) and then reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; nothing senses where the fingers stop.
